ruleName: Ball at rest moved by an outside influence
title: What to do if your ball is moved by an animal
question: A dog runs onto the course and moves your ball from where it was resting. What is the correct action under the Rules?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the dog left it
Replace the ball as close as possible to its original spot, with no penalty
Add a penalty stroke and drop the ball
Skip the hole and move to the next one

explanation: If an outside influence, such as a dog, moves your ball at rest, you must replace it as close as possible to its original spot with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What should you do if an animal moves your ball?
juniorVersion.question: Imagine a dog runs onto the course and kicks your golf ball away from where it was. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the dog left it
Put the ball back to where it was before the dog moved it. No penalty.
Add a penalty and drop the ball
Skip this hole and go to the next one

juniorVersion.explanation: If an animal moves your ball, you should put it back to where it was before. You don’t get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A penalty is an extra shot added to your score because you broke a rule.
Put your ball back where it was before.
Something not part of the game, like an animal, person, or something blowing the ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Explain that if something outside the game (like a dog or bird) moves the ball, golfers always put the ball back where it was.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they have to play the ball from where the animal moved it.
Some may think there is always a penalty when a ball is moved.
